Who We Are

About ST Performance

Twenty years embedded in elite professional sport across four countries and multiple codes, now applied to individuals, departments and organisations who want their performance built by design rather than left to chance.

Founder

Simon Thomas

Simon has spent close to two decades shaping performance systems across international and professional rugby, Major League Baseball and international consulting. His career covers the full arc of high performance work, from building programmes with his own hands to leading multidisciplinary departments where his job is growing the people who deliver.

That arc matters. It means he has lived every seat in the room: the young practitioner with no resources, the department head with a full staff, the advisor guiding a programme from the outside. Whatever seat you are in, he has sat in it.

Simon is a New Zealander based between Perth and the United States, and works with clients worldwide in person and remotely. He writes at @st_performancecoach and on LinkedIn.

The Journey

From the weight room floor to the boardroom

New Zealand

Tasman Mako

Hands-on programme build and delivery

The foundation years, and the ones that shaped everything after. Tasman arrived as the newest union in the competition and, for a long stretch, the easiest to beat. Building a provincial programme with minimal support taught Simon that systems come before resources, and that clarity is the cheapest performance tool there is.

That build ended in the province's first ever title and promotion, taking a side that had been the competition's makeweight and turning it into a regular finalist. Nothing about it was inherited. It was constructed, season by season, by a small group with very little to work with.

New Zealand

Canterbury

Hands-on lead within a fuller support structure

Leading delivery inside one of New Zealand's most successful provincial environments, where his seasonal theming methodology began. The principle set here still holds: the group must own the theme because they helped build it.

New Zealand

Crusaders

Head of a multidisciplinary performance department

Eight years inside the most successful club in Super Rugby history, the final four of them leading the performance department across four consecutive titles. Decentralised delivery through staff, department design and culture work at championship standard.

United States

Austin Gilgronis, Major League Rugby

Director of Performance, built from zero

A full department built from nothing in a start-up league, then deliberately stepped back from as staff grew into it. Simon also operated as de facto assistant general manager, adding roster, operations and commercial perspective to the performance lens.

Australia

Western Force

Performance leadership across Men's, Women's and Academy

Multidisciplinary leadership across three programmes at once, aligning philosophy, staff development and resource allocation across an entire club pathway.

United States

Boston Red Sox

Coordinator, Physical Performance (Player Development)

Leadership, strategy and staff growth across a Major League Baseball player development system, overseeing physical performance staff across seven affiliate locations. All leadership and no athlete-level delivery, by design.

The pattern across every stop is the same. Build the system, grow the people, then hand it over stronger than you found it.
The Record

The career, in numbers.

Four consecutive Super Rugby titles from 2017 to 2020. Every one of them a squad, a coaching group, a performance department and a wider staff, which is the only way any of them happen.
National Honours

Selected, not appointed.

National selection in this profession works differently to a job. You do not apply. You are chosen, usually by people who have watched you work for years, and the appointment says something a title cannot.

Simon was part of the Māori All Blacks performance staff across six matches between 2018 and 2020, and served ten matches with the New Zealand Under 20 side in 2012 and 2013.

The Māori All Blacks environment carries responsibilities that reach past preparation. The team represents whakapapa and a kaupapa considerably older than any fixture, and everyone inside it, staff included, is expected to understand what they are part of and to carry it properly. It remains one of the more significant environments he has worked in.

Across Codes

The problem is the same everywhere.

The work has never been confined to one code. Alongside rugby and baseball, Simon worked with Bowyn Morgan on cognitive training built around decision making under fatigue. Morgan was New Zealand's top ranked welterweight at the time, and the work also covered strength and mobility. In boxing an opening might appear once in ten rounds, so the ability to see it and act while exhausted is the whole game.

The exchange ran both ways. Morgan worked with Crusaders players returning from injury, using boxing based conditioning to rebuild them. That is usually how the best transfer happens, as a trade between practitioners.

Strip away the sport and the question underneath is constant. How does a person make a good decision, under fatigue, when it matters, and everything else is simply the context in which that question gets asked.

Advisory Portfolio

Trusted beyond the building

National Framework Build

Brazil Rugby

A hybrid advisory and delivery engagement building a full national performance framework for sevens and fifteens toward a home Olympics, with quarterly on-ground audit visits.

Remote Advisory

Singapore Rugby

A two-year remote engagement with the General Manager of High Performance and national performance staff, proving that structured advisory support works across time zones.

Leadership Oversight

Panasonic Wild Knights

Leadership oversight of a newly promoted head strength and conditioning coach in Japan, supporting integration across coaching and medical in one of the world's top club environments.

Athlete Advocacy

Director of High Performance

United States Rugby Players Association

Simon was appointed the association's first ever Director of High Performance, a role created to bring performance expertise to the player side of the table. Where most high performance work serves the club, this work serves the athlete: standards of care across the league, welfare, career development and the conditions players are asked to perform in.

It is the clearest expression of the People First value in practice. The same rigour applied to preparing a squad, pointed instead at whether the people inside the system are being looked after well enough to sustain a career in it.
